intro: Learn to say how often you do different activities.
b1.texto:
The usual scale of frequency:

**siempre** → **casi siempre** → **normalmente** → **a menudo** → **a veces** → **casi nunca** → **nunca**

To count how regularly something happens we use: **una vez / dos veces** + **a la semana**, **al mes**, **al año**.
To talk about parts of the day we use **por la tarde**, **por la noche**.
b4.texto: Notice how prepositions are used in fixed expressions of time and frequency.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! Casi nunca shows a very low frequency.
b7.pregunta: Choose the correct combination for the expression of frequency.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct! Una vez a la semana is the standard form.
b7.o1.refuerzo: En la semana is not the usual structure here.
b7.o2.refuerzo: De la semana does not express regularity.
b8.traduccion: I go to the gym twice a week.
p.con qué frecuencia.consejo: A question to find out how regularly something happens.
p.normalmente.consejo: In a habitual or common way.
p.casi siempre.consejo: On the great majority of occasions.
p.una vez a la semana.consejo: Just one day out of every seven.
p.dos veces al mes.consejo: Two occasions every thirty days or so.
p.temprano.consejo: In the first hours of the morning.
b2.f0.texto: How often do you go to the gym?
b2.f1.texto: I go to the gym twice a week.
b2.f2.texto: I usually go for a walk on a quiet afternoon.
b2.f3.texto: On weekdays I always get up early.
b2.f4.texto: And what do you do at weekends?
b2.f5.texto: Sometimes I get up at twelve.
b4.e0.texto: We go for a walk every day in the park.
b4.e1.texto: Pablo goes to the gym twice a month.
b5.f0.texto: Having a healthy routine helps keep the body in good shape.
b5.f1.texto: Pablo goes to the gym twice a week to do physical exercise.
b5.f2.texto: On weekdays he gets up early and goes out running along the wide avenue.
b5.f3.texto: Lucía prefers to walk in the green park, almost always in the afternoon.
b5.f4.texto: He often reads interesting books or listens to relaxing music at home.
b5.f5.texto: At weekends they rest together and almost never go to bed early.
b7.frase: Voy al gimnasio una vez ___ semana.
b8.frase: Voy al gimnasio dos veces a la semana.
p.gimnasio.consejo: The «g» before «i» sounds like an «h»: «him-NA-syo». Don't say a «j» as in English.
p.semana.consejo: Stress the middle: «se-MA-na». With «a la semana» you say how often: «dos veces a la semana», twice a week.
p.paseamos.consejo: From «pasear», which comes from «paso» (step). The ending «-amos» means «we»; say «e» and «a» in separate syllables.
p.mantener.consejo: Built on «tener», so it follows it: «yo mantengo», just like «yo tengo». Stress the last syllable.
p.cuerpo.consejo: The «ue» is one sound: «KWER-po». Related to «corporal» (of the body).
p.buena.consejo: Feminine of «bueno». Before a masculine singular noun it shortens: «buen día».
p.físico.consejo: The tilde is on the first syllable: «FI-si-ko». Don't mix it up with «la física», the science.
p.correr.consejo: The double «rr» is a strong roll: «ko-RRER». Stress the last syllable.
p.avenida.consejo: The «v» sounds like a «b»: «a-be-NI-da». An «avenida» is bigger than a «calle».
p.ancha.consejo: The «ch» sounds as in «chocolate»: «AN-cha». Its opposite is «estrecha».
p.prefiere.consejo: From «preferir»: the stressed «e» becomes «ie» in «prefiero», «prefieres», «prefiere». The «ie» is one sound.
p.interesantes.consejo: Adjectives ending in «-e» are the same for masculine and feminine. The plural just adds «-s».
p.o.consejo: Short and clean, like the «o» in «oso»: just «o». It joins two choices.
p.relajante.consejo: From «relajar», to relax. The «j» sounds like an «h»: «rre-la-HAN-te». The initial «r» is strong.
p.descansan.consejo: From «descansar». The ending «-an» is for «ellos» or «ellas»: they rest.
p.acuestan.consejo: From «acostarse»: the «o» becomes «ue» (as in «acuesta»). The ending «-an» is for «ellos», and «se» goes before it.
p.pronto.consejo: Stress the first syllable: «PRON-to». In this sentence it means early; its opposite is «tarde».
p.tranquila.consejo: The «qu» sounds like a «k» with a silent «u»: «tran-KI-la». The masculine is «tranquilo».
